statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). A seventh consecutive hour after the Globex reopen leaves the 28,981.00-29,100.00 band exactly unchanged, with NQ at 29,013.75 (-1.27%) in the lower third of that band, while the Nikkei has recovered roughly half of a 2% decline off its 62,726.18 low. That combination of range containment and a genuine Asian retracement is the opposite of a no-retracement path, so Tail stays at the bottom of the watch band at 20. Stress eases a point to 76 but remains high on a 4-5% global oil supply outage, Brent above 104, a 10-year near 4.98% at the last cash close and a Wednesday FOMC with projections.
recommendation: Tail remains at the bottom of the watch band and well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is unchanged at 13:00-16:00 UTC, covering the 13:30 UTC US cash open and the first full cash hour, which is the first US auction to price both the weekend AI-pacing story and the Saudi East-West pipeline outage; conditional Tail peaks at 24 there, one point below the block band, because the amplifying structure that would justify crossing it has not been observed. The named invalidation for the constructive structural read is unchanged: a decisive loss of the 28,981.00 reopen low on shallow pullbacks, with the 07:00 UTC European cash open the next scheduled test. Monday's US calendar holds only routine 3-month and 6-month bill auctions at 15:30 UTC. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold an unchanged 28,981-29,100 band for a seventh hour at -1.27% while the Nikkei retraces half its decline and WTI holds 103
body:
A seventh consecutive hour of live price-path evidence leaves the structural read constructive. NQ is quoted at 29,013.75, down 373.25 points or 1.27% against the 29,387.00 reference close, as of 00:16 EDT, and an independent quote on the December contract shows -1.29%, so the move is well corroborated. The decisive structural fact is unchanged: the front-month day range is still exactly 28,981.00 to 29,100.00, the same 119-point band printed in the first hour after the Globex reopen. Seven hours without range expansion, and without a chain of failed retracements, is the opposite of the price path that overwhelms a mean-reversion book.

The new evidence this hour is cross-asset and constructive. The Nikkei 225 traded down to 62,726.18, roughly 2% below its prior close, and has since recovered to 63,356.86, down 1.02%, giving back about half the decline inside the Asian cash session. That is an observed, meaningful retracement in the largest Asian equity pool rather than an assumption, and it is the clearest sign so far that the weekend repricing is being absorbed rather than extended. Against it, NQ has drifted to the lower third of its band, 33 points above the 28,981.00 low, which is why Tail is held rather than cut.

The two drivers behind the gap are unresolved but both are now well documented. Anthropic's Dario Amodei published an essay on 12 September arguing that AI developers should pace the advance of frontier models on safety grounds, and OpenAI's Sam Altman publicly agreed and indicated the company would not pursue a listing this year. That is a sentiment and valuation story for the megacap AI complex that drove index futures lower on the Sunday reopen. Separately, Saudi Arabia shut its 1,200-kilometre East-West pipeline from Abqaiq to Yanbu after drone attacks originating in Iraq; the line had been moving four to five million barrels a day, or roughly 4-5% of global supply, and was the principal route bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, which has been disrupted since March. WTI is at 103.02, up 2.97%, in a 101.59-103.58 session range, with Brent above 104.

Two evidence limitations are worth stating plainly. The VIX at 15.84 and the 10-year at 4.975% are Friday cash closes and therefore predate the weekend news entirely; neither is a live read on current volatility or rates, and the assessment does not treat them as one. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was also unavailable for supporting use this hour, reporting a partial collection roughly 170 minutes old, so this assessment rests on independent primary-source research alone. Confidence is held at 86 on the strength of corroborated price data and verified reporting, tempered by those two gaps.

Forward risk stays concentrated in the 13:00-16:00 UTC stretch around the US cash open, the first deep US auction to price either story, with the 07:00 UTC European open the nearer test. Wednesday's FOMC decision, projections and press conference, preceded the same morning by August retail sales, is the week's structural focus and the main reason Stress stays high while Tail does not.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available. Tail climbed steadily through the weekend from 6 at 04:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC, eased to 16, then stepped through 17, 18, 18 and 19 into the Globex reopen, crossing into the watch band at 21, peaking at 22 in the reopen hour, and settling at 20 for three hours, 19 once, and 20 in the final hour. The mapped state was EA_ON and green for the first 17 hours, then WATCH and yellow for most of the reopen window with a single EA_ON hour at 02:00 UTC. Stress rose without interruption from 60 to 78 as the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop accumulated, then eased to 76-77. Confidence held near 86-87 through the weekend, dropped to 71 for several hours when live price evidence was thin, and rebuilt to 86 once the reopen delivered a continuous price path. Dominant mode was normal for 18 hours, event/whipsaw in the reopen hour, and mixed for the final five.
outlookSummary: Conditional risk stays concentrated in the 13:00-16:00 UTC stretch around the 13:30 UTC US cash open, the first US auction to price both the weekend AI-pacing story and the Saudi East-West pipeline outage. The forecast peaks at Tail 24 in the first full cash hour, one point below the block band, rather than entering it on structure that has not been observed. Two nearer checkpoints precede it: the Japanese cash close near 06:00 UTC, and more importantly the 07:00 UTC European cash open, where conditional Tail rises to 22 as the first deep non-Asian pool to price the story. Between and after them the base case is continued absorption, with Tail decaying to 19 through the European pre-US lull and again across the US afternoon and the Asian Tuesday session. Stress stays in the high band throughout because the supply outage, the rates backdrop and Wednesday's FOMC are unresolved regardless of intraday path. The standing caveat is that every hour beyond the current one describes conditional risk; no future price structure has been observed, and a decisive loss of the 28,981.00 reopen low on shallow pullbacks would invalidate the constructive structural read.
